0.long_answer: Ellis–Van Creveld syndrome is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the EVC gene. This disorder is characterized by features such as short stature, polydactyly (especially postaxial polydactyly of the hands), and abnormalities in the skeletal system. As a ciliopathy, Ellis–Van Creveld syndrome results from defects in the structure and functionality of primary cilia, which play a critical role in various signaling pathways during development. The disruption in ciliary function due to EVC gene mutations underlies the clinical manifestations observed in this syndrome, linking it to the group of diseases known as ciliopathies.
